Settings for the min-p combination

Source: R/minp.R
riposte_minp_control.Rd

The min-p combination (riposte_test(statistic = "minp"), the default) takes the smallest of several p-values at the observed assignment and at every re-randomization, and reports the share of assignments whose smallest p-value is at most the observed one. This function sets which p-values it combines and how each is computed.

Usage

riposte_minp_control(
  pvalue = c("midp", "randomization", "asymptotic"),
  quadratic = NULL,
  block = NULL
)

Arguments

pvalue

how each p-value inside the min-p is computed at every assignment. "midp" (default): the mid-p value of the statistic among the assignments, the share more extreme plus half the share tied. "randomization": the ordinary randomization p-value, the share of assignments at which the statistic is at least as extreme, ties counted in full. "asymptotic": the two-sided normal tail of each standardized statistic (one-sided under a one-sided alternative) and the chi-square tail of the quadratic combination, as in the paper's code. Under every rule the min-p's own p-value comes from the re-randomizations, so the test keeps its level. With "randomization" the min-p's p-value is also at most K times the smallest of its K p-values, so the min-p rejects at level alpha whenever one of them is at or below alpha / K. With "midp" that bound becomes 2K times the smallest mid-p value.

quadratic

whether the quadratic combination's p-value is one of the p-values combined. NULL (default) includes it for a two-sided test and leaves it out for a one-sided test. The quadratic combination squares each representation's departure from its re-randomization mean, so it responds to departures in both directions; asking for it with a one-sided alternative is an error.

block

scores whose block statistic joins the min-p, one more p-value each. The block statistic standardizes a score's treated sum within each block, squares it, and adds the squares over the blocks, so a treatment that raises outcomes in some blocks and lowers them in others does not cancel. Give the names of representations in representations (for example block = "rank") or a named list of score functions (for example block = list(cosine = riposte_cosine), the paper's cosine statistic). NULL (default) adds none. Its p-value follows pvalue; under "asymptotic" it is the chi-square tail on the number of blocks in the sum. It has no one-sided form, is not yet available with covariance adjustment, and is left out, with a message, when the design has one block or only blocks of two units, where it cannot add anything.

Value

a list of class riposte_minp_control with elements pvalue, quadratic, and block, for the minp argument of riposte_test().

Examples

riposte_minp_control()
#> $pvalue
#> [1] "midp"
#> 
#> $quadratic
#> NULL
#> 
#> $block
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "riposte_minp_control"
riposte_minp_control(pvalue = "randomization")
#> $pvalue
#> [1] "randomization"
#> 
#> $quadratic
#> NULL
#> 
#> $block
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "riposte_minp_control"
riposte_minp_control(quadratic = FALSE)
#> $pvalue
#> [1] "midp"
#> 
#> $quadratic
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $block
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "riposte_minp_control"
riposte_minp_control(block = list(cosine = riposte_cosine))
#> $pvalue
#> [1] "midp"
#> 
#> $quadratic
#> NULL
#> 
#> $block
#> $block$cosine
#> function (y) 
#> {
#>     cos(pi * rank(y, ties.method = "average")/(length(y) + 1))
#> }
#> <bytecode: 0x5cc8a0261e20>
#> <environment: namespace:riposte>
#> 
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "riposte_minp_control"
